newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WRIGHT DOUBLE STRIKE BOOSTS ENGLAND CLAIM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WRIGHT DOUBLE STRIKE BOOSTS ENGLAND CLAIM.

text.p: A double strike by the predatory Ian Wright shot Arsenal to a 2-0 victory over Coventry at Highbury on Monday and strengthened his claim to injured Alan Shearer's England shirt against Moldova next month.

The Arsenal hit-man now has three goals from his first two matches of the season, making him favourite to partner Manchester United's Teddy Sheringham when Moldova visit Wembley for the World Cup qualifier on September 10.
Les Ferdinand is Wright's main rival for the England job but it may take him time to find form after his six million pounds ($9.5 million) move to Tottenham from Newcastle in the close season.
Wright's goals left him just one short of Cliff Bastin's all-time Arsenal scoring record of 178 set in the 1930s and 40s.
Coventry, conquerors of Chelsea in their opening match on Saturday, looked ragged and jaded as Arsene Wenger's European imports ran the show from the start.
Arsenal's Dutch winger Marc Overmars caused constant havoc in the Coventry defence and on the half-hour Wright made the pressure count.
A thumping header from defender Scott Marshall rattled off the Coventry bar and was cleared to Patrick Vieira on the edge of the penalty area.
The Frenchman rifled in a low shot which bobbled out of Coventry 'keeper Steve Ogrizovic's grasp for Wright to pounce from five metres and open the scoring.
Coventry grimly held on until halftime but two minutes after the break Wright again punished the visitors for sloppy defending.
Defender Richard Shaw was hustled out of possession by Wright 40 metres out and the England striker ran on to guide the ball past the advancing Ogrizovic for 2-0.
The victory gave Arsenal four points from their first two matches.

In the League Cup first round, first leg a brace of goals from Dutch striker Pierre van Hooijdonk, Swedish defender Jon Olave Hjelde and Dean Saunders helped first division Nottingham Forest to an 8-0 thrashing of division three Doncaster.
